title: Halden Systems teases Meridian, its next-gen scheduling platform
snippet: Halden Systems used its winter partner call to trail a platform codenamed Meridian, aimed at logistics scheduling. No date, no pricing, and executives declined to say whether it replaces the ageing Corbel suite.

title: Meridian private beta opens to 40 design partners
snippet: Forty companies now have hands on Meridian. Halden says the beta covers scheduling and capacity planning, with the migration tooling landing later.

title: Analysts peg Meridian below $3,000 per seat
snippet: Two analyst notes this week put Meridian in the $2,400 to $2,900 per seat range, reasoning from Corbel's current list price. Halden has not commented on pricing.

title: Halden hires a platform VP ahead of the Meridian rollout
snippet: Halden Systems has hired a VP of Platform from a rival scheduling vendor, a signal that the Meridian rollout is being taken seriously internally.

title: Meridian pilot lands at a Pune logistics firm
snippet: A mid-sized Pune freight operator has become the first named Meridian pilot outside Halden's home market. The pilot covers depot scheduling only.

title: Beta users say Meridian's migration tool is rough
snippet: Design partners report that moving Corbel schedules into Meridian still needs hand-holding. Halden acknowledges the migration tool is incomplete.

title: Halden confirms a summer launch window for Meridian
snippet: Halden has confirmed Meridian will ship in summer, without naming a date or a price. The company says pricing will be announced closer to general availability.

title: Halden schedules a Meridian launch event
snippet: Invitations went out this morning for a Meridian launch event. Halden still has not named a ship date or a price.

title: Meridian pricing, explained
snippet: Meridian lists at $4,900 per seat on an annual commitment, with volume breaks above 500 seats. Halden positions this well above the outgoing Corbel suite.

title: Who actually owns Halden Systems now?
snippet: Following the Ferrous Labs deal, Halden's roadmap commitments are being re-examined by customers who signed multi-year Meridian contracts.

title: A first look at Meridian capacity planning
snippet: The capacity planning module is the part of Meridian design partners keep asking about. This is what it looks like in the current beta build.

title: Meridian to ship October 14 at $4,900 per seat
snippet: Halden Systems has named October 14 as the Meridian general availability date and set list pricing at $4,900 per seat per year, well above analyst expectations.

title: Meridian goes live, Halden claims 1,240 seats in week one
snippet: Meridian reached general availability on October 14. Halden says 1,240 seats sold in the first week, mostly conversions from the Corbel suite.

title: Ferrous Labs acquires Halden Systems for $310 million
snippet: Ferrous Labs has agreed to buy Halden Systems for $310 million in cash and stock, six weeks after the Meridian launch.

title: Meridian outage knocks out scheduling for three customers
snippet: A six-hour Meridian outage left three large customers unable to schedule depot slots. Ferrous Labs, which now owns Halden, declined to comment.
